raw_case_text: A 7-year-old girl presented to our hospital with fever and tender right cervical lymphadenopathy of 20-day duration. She underwent surgery for Pierre-Robin syndrome when she was 2 years old. She was noted to have a tender right cervical lymphadenopathy of >2 cm in diameter without hepatosplenomegaly. On admission, her CRP level was normal. The complete blood count revealed a WBC count of 4,410 cells/mm3 and an ESR of 92 mm/h. EBV, CMV, and HBV serum tests were negative. An excisional cervical lymph node biopsy was performed, which showed paracortical hyperplasia accompanied by a large number of immunoblastic macrocells revealing KFD. The patient was treated with NSAIDs. After 14 days, her fever resolved with regression of the noted lymphadenopathy. The inflammatory markers remain elevated. The patient was discharged with naproxen, hydroxychloroquine, and a tapering dose of prednisone. Four months later, she had a 30-day history of rapidly progressive hyposthenia, ataxic gait, and urinary retention. The patient was brought to our emergency department due to status epilepticus, which presented as generalized tonic-clonic seizures with unconsciousness, lock-jaw, and blank stare. Oxygen support was provided, and intravenous diazepam and midazolam were administered. Physical and neurological examinations revealed hyperextension of the limbs. No other abnormalities were noted. Head computed tomography on admission revealed decreased white matter density. CSF analysis revealed an elevated number of cells (42/mm3, 82% lymphocytes) and proteins (22.7 mg/dL). The CSF sample was submitted for bacteriologic and viral examination and evaluated with serological and pathological tests. Growth was not observed in the non-specific or mycotic cultures of the CSF sample. The patient was diagnosed with encephalopathy associated with KFD. IVIG (1 g/kg) and an intravenous bolus dose of methylprednisolone (360 mg/d for 3 days) were administered. Plasma exchange was performed two times. After 4 weeks of treatment, the child was still unable to speak or sit without support. MRI findings showed remaining symmetrical abnormal signals in the bilateral basal ganglia with no apparent changes. The prognosis was poor.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 7-year-old girl presented with a 20-day history of fever and tender right cervical lymphadenopathy, and re-presented 4 months later with a 30-day history of rapidly progressive weakness, gait ataxia, urinary retention, and acute status epilepticus.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Admitted initially after 20 days of fever and tender right cervical lymphadenopathy (>2 cm), the patient was diagnosed with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease (KFD) via excisional lymph node biopsy and discharged after 14 days on naproxen, hydroxychloroquine, and tapering prednisone. Four months later, following 30 days of progressive hyposthenia, ataxic gait, and urinary retention, she presented to the emergency department in generalized tonic-clonic status epilepticus with coma and trismus.
subjective.past_medical_history: Pierre-Robin syndrome status post corrective surgery at age 2 years.
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial episode: 20 days of fever and tender right neck swelling. Relapse 4 months later: 30 days of progressive generalized weakness (hyposthenia), gait ataxia, urinary retention, and acute generalized tonic-clonic status epilepticus.

objective.physical_examination: Initial admission: febrile with a tender right cervical lymph node >2 cm in diameter and no hepatosplenomegaly. Readmission 4 months later: unconscious with blank stare, trismus (lock-jaw), generalized tonic-clonic status epilepticus, and four-limb hyperextension.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial admission: normal CRP, WBC 4,410 cells/mm3, markedly elevated ESR 92 mm/h, and negative serum tests for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), and hepatitis B virus (HBV).
objective.advanced_workup: Excisional right cervical lymph node biopsy demonstrated paracortical hyperplasia with abundant immunoblastic macrocells diagnostic of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease (KFD). Readmission head CT showed decreased cerebral white matter density, and brain MRI revealed persistent symmetrical abnormal signal intensities in the bilateral basal ganglia. Lumbar puncture revealed CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis (42 cells/mm3, 82% lymphocytes) and protein 22.7 mg/dL, with negative bacterial, fungal, and viral CSF cultures and serologies.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease (KFD; confirmed by excisional cervical lymph node biopsy with negative EBV, CMV, and HBV testing) complicated 4 months later by severe KFD-associated autoimmune/inflammatory encephalopathy and bilateral basal ganglia lesions presenting with ataxia, urinary retention, and status epilepticus. Despite airway support, IV diazepam/midazolam, high-dose IVIG (1 g/kg), pulse IV methylprednisolone (360 mg/day for 3 days), and two sessions of plasma exchange, after 4 weeks of treatment the child remained unable to speak or sit unsupported with persistent bilateral basal ganglia lesions on MRI.
